classic.tagline: Accounts kept in good order, and advice you can act on
classic.intro: Chartered accountants for small businesses, landlords and the self-employed across Bath and north Somerset.
classic.about_title: A small practice that knows your name
classic.about:
Margaret Hartwell opened the practice above a bookshop on Milsom Street in 1998. Daniel Finch joined as a trainee and became a partner twelve years later. We are still a small firm on purpose.

You deal with the same accountant all year, not a call centre. We explain what the numbers mean in plain English, tell you what is due and when, and agree our fee before any work begins.

services.name: Year-end accounts
services.description: Accounts prepared, explained and filed on time for sole traders, partnerships and limited companies.

services.name: Self assessment
services.description: Your tax return completed and checked, with a clear note of what to pay and when.

services.name: Bookkeeping and VAT
services.description: Monthly or quarterly bookkeeping and VAT returns filed through Making Tax Digital software.

services.name: Payroll
services.description: Payslips, pensions and submissions handled for teams of one to fifty.

services.name: Landlord accounts
services.description: Rental income, allowable costs and capital gains worked out properly for one property or twenty.

services.name: Business advice
services.description: Help with starting up, taking on staff, buying premises or planning to sell.

values.title: One accountant, all year
values.text: You always know who is looking after your affairs and how to reach them.

values.title: Fees agreed first
values.text: We quote a fixed fee before we start, so the invoice is never a surprise.

values.title: Plain English
values.text: We explain what we have done and why, without the jargon.

process.title: A free first meeting
process.text: Half an hour, in person or by video, to understand your business and what you need.

process.title: A fixed quote
process.text: We write down exactly what we will do and what it will cost each year.

process.title: We take over the paperwork
process.text: We contact your previous accountant and HMRC so you do not have to.

process.title: Regular check-ins
process.text: We remind you of every deadline and review your position before the year ends.

faq.q: How do I switch accountant?
faq.a: Tell us who you use now and sign one letter. We request your records from them and register with HMRC as your agent. It normally takes about two weeks.

faq.q: Do I have to come to your office?
faq.a: No. Around half our clients work with us entirely by email, phone and video. You are always welcome to call in.

faq.q: What software do you use?
faq.a: We support Xero, FreeAgent and QuickBooks, and can set one up for you. If you prefer a spreadsheet, that is fine too.

faq.q: When will I know what tax I owe?
faq.a: For most clients, within four weeks of sending us your records, and always well before the payment date.

projects.details: The owner had been a sole trader for four years. We moved the business to a limited company, registered for PAYE, set up a workplace pension and trained the manager to approve payroll each month.

projects.title: Eleven rental flats, one clear picture
projects.summary: Untangled five years of rental records and reduced the tax bill legitimately.
projects.details: Records were spread across three letting agents. We rebuilt the figures property by property, claimed finance costs and repairs that had been missed, and set up a simple quarterly routine.

projects.summary: Three years of planning so the owner could retire on good terms.
projects.details: We tidied the balance sheet, documented the order book and worked with the solicitor on the sale. The business was sold to its manager.

projects.summary: Moved a busy café from paper receipts to Xero in a month.
projects.details: We connected the till and bank feed, photographed the backlog of receipts and showed the owner how to check the week's figures in ten minutes.

bold.intro: MOTs, servicing and repairs for every make of car and van. Straight prices, no surprises, on Kirkstall Road in Leeds.
bold.about_title: Three brothers. One garage. No nonsense.
bold.about:
Our dad opened Redline in 1987 with one ramp and a kettle. We grew up sweeping the floor here. Today there are nine bays, eleven technicians and the same rule: show the customer the problem before you fix it.

We photograph every fault, price every job before we start and never fit a part you do not need. If we would not do it to our own car, we will not do it to yours.

services.description: Class 4 and class 7 tests. Free re-test within ten working days.

services.name: Full service
services.description: A 60-point check with oil, filters and a written health report.

services.name: Brakes
services.description: Pads, discs and fluid, fitted and road-tested the same day.

services.name: Clutch and gearbox
services.description: Clutch replacement and gearbox repairs with a 12-month guarantee.

services.name: Diagnostics
services.description: Dealer-level fault finding for warning lights and electrical problems.

services.name: Tyres and tracking
services.description: Budget to premium tyres fitted while you wait, with four-wheel alignment.

values.title: See it before we fix it
values.text: We send photos of every fault so you can decide with the facts in front of you.

values.title: The quote is the price
values.text: If we find something else, we call you before we touch it.

values.title: Guaranteed for a year
values.text: Every repair carries a 12-month parts and labour guarantee.

process.title: Book a slot
process.text: Online or by phone. Same-week appointments most weeks.

process.title: Drop it off
process.text: Leave the keys and take a free courtesy car if you need one.

process.title: We call with the facts

process.title: Collect and go
process.text: Pay on collection and keep the old parts if you want to see them.

faq.q: Can I wait while you do the MOT?
faq.a: Yes. It takes about 45 minutes and there is a waiting room with coffee and wifi.

faq.q: Do you work on electric and hybrid cars?
faq.a: Yes. Four of our technicians are qualified to work on high-voltage systems.

faq.q: Will a service here affect my warranty?
faq.a: No. We service to the manufacturer's schedule with approved parts, which keeps your warranty valid.

faq.q: How do I pay?
faq.a: Card, cash or bank transfer on collection. We can spread larger repairs over three months.

minimal.tagline: Tableware thrown by hand in Leith
minimal.intro: Plates, bowls and cups made in small batches, and wheel classes for beginners in our studio by the water.
minimal.about_title: One potter, one wheel, a lot of plates
minimal.about:
Ingrid Oda trained in Kyoto and Stoke-on-Trent before opening the studio in 2016. Everything is thrown on the wheel, trimmed by hand and glazed in one of three colours mixed in the studio.

The work is made to be used every day. It stacks, it goes in the dishwasher, and it gets better with a few years of breakfasts behind it.

services.description: Two and a half hours at the wheel. We fire and glaze your two best pieces.

services.name: Six-week course
services.description: One evening a week, from centring clay to a finished set of bowls.

services.name: Tableware
services.description: Plates, bowls, cups and jugs from the current batch, in the shop and online.

services.name: Restaurant commissions
services.description: Tableware designed with your kitchen and made in runs of forty or more.

services.name: Private sessions
services.description: The studio to yourselves for birthdays and small groups of up to eight.

values.title: Small batches
values.text: No more than sixty pieces in a firing, each one checked by hand.

values.title: Made to be used

process.title: Throw
process.text: Each piece is shaped on the wheel from a weighed ball of clay.

process.title: Trim
process.text: A day later the foot is cut and the surface smoothed.

process.title: Fire

faq.q: When do I get my pieces?

faq.q: Can it go in the dishwasher?
faq.a: Yes. All our tableware is dishwasher and microwave safe.

faq.q: Do you sell gift vouchers?
faq.a: Yes, for classes or for the shop. They are valid for a year.

playful.tagline: Happy dogs, fresh haircuts, zero stress
playful.intro: Gentle grooming and fun-packed day care for dogs of every shape and fluff level, five minutes from Brighton seafront.

playful.about:
Waggy Tails started in Jess's spare room with one very patient spaniel called Biscuit. Eight years on we have a bright shop in Kemptown, four groomers and a garden for the day care gang.

We only ever groom one dog at a time, we never use cages, and nervous dogs get as many breaks and biscuits as they need.

modern.about:
Pixel Fix opened in 2017 in a unit the size of a lift. We now have a bright workshop on Oldham Street and six technicians who would rather mend a phone than sell you a new one.

Every repair has a fixed price, quality parts and a 12-month warranty. If we cannot fix it, you do not pay.

faq.q: How long will it take?
faq.a: Screens and batteries usually take 30 to 60 minutes. Water damage and laptops can take a day or two.

faq.q: Will I lose my data?
faq.a: Almost never. Screen and battery repairs do not touch your data. We still recommend a backup first.

faq.q: Do you use genuine parts?
faq.a: We offer genuine parts where they are available and high-quality alternatives at a lower price. You choose.

faq.q: What does the warranty cover?
faq.a: Any fault with the part or our work for 12 months. It does not cover new accidental damage.

rustic.tagline: Grown down the lane, baked this morning
rustic.intro: A family farm shop and café near Ledbury selling our own fruit, vegetables, cider and bread, with breakfast served until noon.
rustic.about_title: The same family, the same fields, since 1921
rustic.about:
The Pembertons have grown apples at Orchard Lane for more than a hundred years. The shop began as a table at the gate with an honesty box. The table is still there, in the corner by the till.

Today we sell what we grow, what our neighbours make and what Nan bakes. If it has travelled more than thirty miles to reach the shelf, we have had a long argument about it.

editorial.tagline: Flowers for weddings that look like the season they are in
editorial.intro: A Cotswold studio making loose, garden-led flowers for weddings and gatherings, grown here or within a morning's drive.
editorial.trust_line: Wedding and event florist, the Cotswolds
editorial.about_title: A cutting garden, a barn and a very full diary
editorial.about:
Clara Rye left a career in publishing to grow flowers in a walled garden outside Stow-on-the-Wold. The studio now takes on twenty weddings a year, so that each one has her full attention.

We work with what the season offers: blossom and tulips in spring, roses and sweet peas in June, dahlias and grasses in autumn. Nothing is flown in and nothing is arranged in foam.

services.name: Full wedding flowers
services.description: Ceremony, reception and everything carried or worn, designed around your venue and month.

services.name: Bridal party only
services.description: Bouquets, buttonholes and flower crowns for smaller celebrations.

services.name: Installations
services.description: Arches, hanging clouds and staircases built on site the day before.

services.name: Supper clubs and events
services.description: Table flowers for private dinners, launches and editorial shoots.

services.name: Buckets of flowers
services.description: Seasonal stems by the bucket for those arranging their own.

services.name: Workshops
services.description: A morning in the garden learning to arrange a hand-tied bouquet.

values.title: In season, always
values.text: Your flowers reflect the month you marry in, not a photograph from another one.

values.title: Grown, not flown
values.text: Nine in ten stems are cut within fifty miles of the studio.

values.title: Foam free
values.text: Everything is arranged in water, moss and reusable frames.

process.title: A conversation
process.text: We talk about your venue, your month and the feeling you want in the room.

process.title: A proposal
process.text: A written design with a palette, a list of likely flowers and a clear price.

process.title: A walk through
process.text: We visit the venue together six weeks before to settle every detail.

process.title: The day itself
process.text: We arrive early, stay until everything is right and return to clear.

faq.q: How far ahead should we book?
faq.a: Most couples book nine to fourteen months ahead. We take one wedding a weekend.

faq.q: Can we choose exact flowers?
faq.a: We agree a palette and a mood, then choose the best of what is flowering that week. It always looks better.

faq.q: Do you travel?
faq.a: Yes, within about ninety minutes of Stow-on-the-Wold. Further by arrangement.

faq.q: What happens to the flowers afterwards?
faq.a: Guests are encouraged to take them home. Anything left goes to a local hospice.
